concepts.title: Prime Factorisation
concepts.definition: The process of expressing a composite number as a product of its prime factors until no further division is possible.
concepts.key_idea: Every composite number has a unique set of prime factors regardless of the order of multiplication.

concepts.title: Highest Common Factor (HCF)
concepts.definition: The greatest number that divides two or more given numbers exactly without leaving any remainder.
concepts.formula: hcf = product of common prime factors with minimum powers
concepts.key_idea: The HCF is the largest shared divisor found by identifying common subparts in prime factorisations.

concepts.title: Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
concepts.definition: The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of two or more given numbers.
concepts.formula: lcm = product of all prime factors with maximum powers
concepts.key_idea: The LCM must contain the prime factorisation of every number in the set as a subpart.

concepts.title: Simultaneous Division Method
concepts.definition: An efficient algorithm to find both HCF and LCM by dividing multiple numbers together by their common factors.
concepts.formula: hcf = product of common divisors; lcm = hcf * product of remaining quotients
concepts.key_idea: Common factors are divided out first for HCF, then remaining factors are handled for LCM.

solution_steps.explain: Divide all numbers by a shared factor (prime or composite) and write the quotients.
The product of all factors used to divide all numbers simultaneously is the HCF.
Continue dividing until no two numbers share a factor, then multiply HCF by all remaining quotients.

concepts.title: HCF and LCM Product Property
concepts.definition: The mathematical relationship stating that the product of the HCF and LCM of two numbers equals the product of the numbers themselves.
concepts.key_idea: This property allows finding the LCM if the HCF and the numbers are known, and vice versa.

concepts.title: Properties of Co-prime Numbers
concepts.definition: Pairs of numbers that have no common factor other than 1.
concepts.key_idea: For co-prime numbers, the LCM is simply the product of the two numbers.
